subject: Tri-continent handoff & ops runbook demo — scheduling
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Saito <alex.saito@acme-finance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Tri-continent handoff & ops runbook demo — scheduling

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, Acme would like an operational deep-dive that covers:
- Multi-region deployment model (EU/US/APAC) and data residency guardrails
- Failover and routing policies (what happens on region outage)
- KV/cache behavior and expected latency/cost tradeoffs by region
- Runbook walkthrough for handoffs between Acme on-call and Redwood SREs

We think the best format is a two-part session: a 45-min tech/architecture walkthrough + a 30-min ops/handoff run-through with live Q&A. To make scheduling easy across timezones, here are a few options (all in UTC):
- Tue 2028-03-14 15:00–16:15 UTC (friendly for US/EU overlap)
- Wed 2028-03-15 01:00–02:15 UTC (APAC early morning)
- Thu 2028-03-16 09:00–10:15 UTC (EU morning / US late-night)

Can you share which slot works best and whether Maria from CloudPartner should join for the infra mapping? Also loop Ops (ops-eng) if they want a dedicated segment.

I'll attach the preliminary runbook and a short agenda in the follow-up.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: tri-continent-agenda.md (markdown, 12KB)]

From: Alex Saito <alex.saito@acme-finance.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops-eng@acme-finance.com>
Date: 2028-03-11T02:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Tri-continent handoff & ops runbook demo — scheduling

Hi Sean —

Appreciate the clear plan. We want both the architecture and runbook walkthroughs, but two small asks: 1) split the session so APAC colleagues can attend a dedicated short window (they're usually offline for late-night US times), and 2) include Maria Tanaka from CloudPartner — they will own the private link and region failover mapping on their side.

Available here (all in UTC):
- Wed 2028-03-15 01:00–02:00 (works for APAC engineers)
- Thu 2028-03-16 09:00–10:30 (we can do a longer joint session)
- Fri 2028-03-17 14:00–15:30 (backup)

If we split, I propose: 30m APAC-friendly session focused on traffic routing and residency, then a 60m joint session for runbook and handoff. Ops attached a short list of questions in the cc.

—Alex
Alex Saito
Platform Engineering Manager, Acme Financial Services

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Tri-continent handoff & ops runbook demo — scheduling

Sean / Karthik —

Agree with Alex that splitting makes the most sense operationally. Quick internal notes before we confirm with Acme:
- Karthik: can you run the architecture half (45m) and highlight the model placement options + quantization/latency implications per region?
- Mina: will handle the runbook/handoff segment — need to confirm SRE on-call overlap windows.
- We should produce a one-page cut of the runbook for the APAC session focusing only on data flow and failover triggers.

Proposed internal plan (UTC):
- Wed 2028-03-15 01:00–01:30 — APAC-focused: data residency & failover (Karthik short + Q&A)
- Thu 2028-03-16 09:00–10:15 — Joint runbook + handoff (Mina lead + Karthik deep-dive)

If that works, Sean please propose those exact times back to Alex and include Maria. I'll prepare the APAC cut next business day and attach it.

Marissa
Director, Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks — I can cover the architecture sections. Attaching the first-pass runbook and a short diagram set for the APAC cut. Notes:
- APAC session: I will keep the architecture portion to ~15–20 minutes and focus only on region routing, KV-locality, and quantization impacts.
- Joint session: I'll expand on kernel selection, batch sizing by region, and expected tail latency numbers so Ops can dimension alert thresholds.

Attachments:
- MR-handoff-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook, 1.8MB)
- tri-region-diagrams.png (svg, 450KB)

I am available for the proposed Wed 2028-03-15 01:00–01:30 and Thu 2028-03-16 09:00–10:15 UTC.

Karthik

Subject: Confirmed: APAC cut + joint runbook session (calendar invites sent)

Alex / Maria / Ops —

Thanks for the quick replies. We will run the sessions as follows (calendar invites sent):
1) APAC cut — Wed 2028-03-15 01:00–01:30 UTC
   - Focus: data residency flow, region failover triggers, APAC-specific networking notes
   - Presenters: Karthik (architecture highlight), Marissa (APAC runbook one-pager)

2) Full runbook + ops handoff — Thu 2028-03-16 09:00–10:15 UTC
   - Focus: end-to-end runbook, SLO/alert thresholds, on-call handoff process, DocuSign/RBAC for access
   - Presenters: Mina (runbook walkthrough), Karthik (deep metrics + kernel/batching implications), Sean (operational handoff and next steps)

What I attached:
- MR-handoff-runbook-v1.pdf (detailed runbook)
- tri-continent-agenda.md (agenda and timeboxed sections)

Action items before sessions:
- Alex / Ops: send any final top-10 questions you want covered by EOD Tue 2028-03-14 UTC.
- Maria: can you confirm if CloudPartner will present the private link failover mapping (we'll reserve 15 minutes)?
- Marissa / Mina / Karthik: I'll need the APAC one-pager and diagram set by Tue 2028-03-14 18:00 UTC so I can attach to invites.

Thanks — see you on the call.

Sean Gallagher
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
